blocking_decision_required.decision: Option 2 - reviewed spec change to the AC5 threshold, taken 2026-09-08.
blocking_decision_required.rationale: spec.md:247 prescribes exactly this path; spec.md:368 records the business priority as compatibility plus a speed-up, not a specific percentage. Thresholds were set with headroom below the measured values so the gate stays falsifiable, and deliberately NOT set to the measured values.
blocking_decision_required.unchanged: AC6 and all compatibility criteria (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC7/AC12) were not touched and pass as originally written. AC8/AC9/AC10 native promotion thresholds are unchanged and still measured against the frozen candidate.

frozen_candidate.note: Frozen as the optimized-Cython comparison point for TASK-17..TASK-20 despite the AC5 shortfall.

AC1_AC2_AC4_AC7_compatibility.note: Two correctness gaps found by adversarial review (metaclass eligibility spoof; a restored __fields__ guard) were fixed BEFORE this run, and each now has a regression test.

AC5_construction_improvement.note: Passes on the CONSERVATIVE end of the 95% interval, not merely the point estimate, so the result is not marginal. The generic-dispatch elimination remains complete: 0 dispatches for unconstrained scalars, 2 for Employee's two ineligible non-scalar fields.
AC5_construction_improvement.spec_amendment: AC5 revised 2026-09-08 under spec.md's own clause 'If AC3/AC5 cannot be met compatibly, report the measured limit and revise the specification through review.' Approved by Jesus Lara (spec owner). Original target 20% recorded in Amendment 1 alongside the measured limit and the reason it is unreachable compatibly.

headline: ALL GATES PASS against the specification as amended. AC5 was revised through review on 2026-09-08 (spec Amendment 1) from a flat 20% Employee target to 8% Employee raw/native plus 12% for all-unconstrained scalar models, after the measured limit was reported and the 20% target was shown to be unreachable compatibly. Measured: Employee raw 9.58% (conservative CI end 8.86%), native 9.91% (9.34%), unconstrained scalars 16.03% (15.42%) -- all clear on the conservative end of the interval. AC6 PASS (worst regression class_creation +4.35% median / +4.54% p95). AC3 PASS. Compatibility PASS with zero divergences everywhere.

history.effect: class_creation +4.91% -> +4.35% with the CI upper bound falling from 5.72% to 4.64%, which is what clears AC6. Employee improvement moved slightly the other way (10.6% -> 9.6%): the `==` diversion check is a rich comparison per gated field and is required for correctness, so this is a deliberate trade of ~1% for behavioural fidelity.
history.note: Second acceptance run. The first (before remediation) failed AC5 AND AC6.
history.what_changed: Removed the duplicate build_field_policy call (abstract.py:356) that TASK-16's own diagnosis identified; stopped allocating a fresh empty frozenset per unconstrained field; plus correctness fixes from adversarial code review (identity-based policy eligibility, checked FieldPolicy cast, restored the __fields__ guard TASK-15 wrongly removed, and mirrored legacy's `value == _type` diversion check instead of `is`).

measurement_quality.note: A 20% effect is comfortably resolvable (worst resolvable 1.24%), so the AC5 shortfall is a real result. class_creation's +4.35% is well above the 1.55% cross-build floor, so it is a real regression -- just now within budget.

noise.guidance: spec §4: if machine noise prevents distinguishing a 5% regression, rerun in a controlled environment rather than declare success. A calibration spread above 10% means this machine was not quiet; treat every inconclusive verdict as 'measure again', not 'no change'.

noise_floor.definition: half-width of the 95% bootstrap interval on the paired median ratio, expressed as a fraction of 1.0
noise_floor.guidance: an effect smaller than the worst resolvable effect must be reported as inconclusive and re-measured in a quieter environment, never rounded into a claim

multiple_comparisons.caution: each verdict uses an independent 95% interval, so across 15 workloads roughly 0.8 spurious 'regression' or 'improvement' labels are expected per run by chance alone. A single flagged workload whose effect is near the noise floor is not evidence; look for an effect that is large relative to the resolvable effect, or that reproduces across independent runs.

calibration.note: pure-Python integer loop, independent of datamodel; a process whose calibration deviates from the median indicates CPU frequency scaling or core migration, not a code change

reproduce: python benchmarks/model_performance.py --pin-cpu <cpu> --control-root <second independently built worktree of d932c720> --output <out>.json

same_source_control.conclusion: treat any movement within the empirical cross-build floor as no change, regardless of what its confidence interval says. A single workload flagged near this floor is not evidence; a real result must be large relative to it and reproduce across runs.

noise.guidance: spec §4: if machine noise prevents distinguishing a 5% regression, rerun in a controlled environment rather than declare success. A calibration spread above 10% means this machine was not quiet; treat every inconclusive verdict as 'measure again', not 'no change'.

same_source_control.purpose: calibration: both sides are the SAME commit built independently, so the true ratio is 1.0 everywhere. Anything else this reports is harness noise plus binary-layout effects.
